headline: Most people listen to respond, not to understand
universal_truth: True listening is one of the rarest and most valuable gifts we can give
fun_facts: Studies show we remember only 25-50% of what we hear—and less when we're planning our response
Active listening can reduce misunderstandings by up to 80% in workplace settings
The average person speaks at 125 words per minute, but we can process 400—leaving room for distraction
discussion_questions: Who in your life makes you feel truly heard?
What stops you from listening fully?
How does it feel when someone really listens to you?

hook.script: Here's a test: in your last conversation, were you really listening—or were you waiting for your turn to talk? Most of us are thinking about what we'll say next while others are still speaking. Today, we learn why that's a problem and how to fix it.

cliff.script: We speak at about 125 words per minute, but our brains can process 400. That gap is where our attention wanders—to our phones, our to-do list, our brilliant comeback. How do great listeners stay present?
cliff.prompt: What's the key to truly listening?

options.response: Exactly. Listening to understand, rather than to reply, changes everything.

options.text: Don't interrupt and maintain eye contact
options.response: Those help, but there's something deeper...

fact1.title: The Retention Problem
fact1.script: Immediately after a conversation, we remember only 50% of what was said. After 48 hours? Just 25%. And that's when we're trying. When we're planning our response while others speak, retention drops even further. Listening takes intention.

fact2.title: The Gap That Wanders
fact2.script: We process speech 3 times faster than people can talk. That cognitive surplus should help us think deeper about what we're hearing. Instead, our minds drift to distractions. Great listeners use that gap to seek understanding, not escape.

fact3.title: The Power of Being Heard
fact3.script: When people feel truly listened to, their stress hormones decrease and they become more creative and collaborative. Listening isn't just nice—it changes the speaker's brain chemistry. Your attention is a gift with real effects.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Listening is not waiting. It's not silence while you prepare to speak. Real listening is putting aside your own agenda and genuinely seeking to understand another human being. It's surprisingly rare—and surprisingly powerful.

outro.script: That's Day 10—our first ten days complete. Thank you for listening to me. Tomorrow, we begin a new chapter. Until then, practice the gift of your full attention.

growTrack.title: Full Presence - Listening Practice
growTrack.learning_objective: Develop the skill of listening without planning a response
growTrack.activity: In one conversation today, practice this: After the other person finishes speaking, count to 2 in your head before responding. Use that pause to make sure you understood, not to prepare your reply.
